### Problem: list the root-to-leaf paths {#sec-tr-p3-paths}

::: {.p-statement}
Return every root-to-leaf path as a string of node values joined by `"->"`. Any order is accepted.

Constraints: $1 \le n \le 100$.

Source: [LC 257 · Binary Tree Paths](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-paths/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The text of the path is the state. A leaf emits it. Passing a new string down copies the whole path at every node. One shared list, with the node pushed before the children and popped after them, copies each path only when a leaf emits it.
:::

::: {#fig-tr-paths}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):

    root = V.Node("1", [
        V.Node("2", [V.Node("5", note="1->2->5")]),
        V.Node("3", note="1->3"),
    ])
    V.tree(ax, p, root, dx=1.6, dy=1.4, size=10)

V.show(draw)
```

The sample has two leaves, so two strings. The missing left child of $2$ is not a path.

:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Shared path.** Append the value, emit at a leaf, pop on the way out. Every exit pops, including the leaf's `return`. Skipping that pop glues the next path onto the previous one.
2. **By value.** Build `path + "->" + val` for the child. Same strings, more copying. Fine at $n \le 100$, and the form people write first.
3. **Parent pointers.** One walk stores `parent[child] = node`. For each leaf, walk up to the root and reverse. Same strings, and the parent array is the tool of the next pattern. `[-1,-2]` is the string `"-1->-2"`.

**Invariant.** When the call is at $v$, the shared list is the root-to-$v$ path, and it has the same contents after the call returns.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Shared path

::: {.form-next}
One list for the whole walk. The pop is what makes the sibling see the parent's path rather than this node's.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('paths', 'shared')
    assert str(final) == "['1->2->5', '1->3']"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def binary_tree_paths(root):
    out, path = [], []

    def walk(u):
        path.append(str(u.val))
        if u.left is None and u.right is None:
            out.append("->".join(path))
        if u.left:
            walk(u.left)
        if u.right:
            walk(u.right)
        path.pop()

    if root:
        walk(root)
    return out
```

##### C++

```cpp
void walkPaths(TreeNode* u, string& cur, vector<string>& out) {
    string add = (cur.empty() ? "" : "->") + to_string(u->val);
    cur += add;
    if (!u->left && !u->right) out.push_back(cur);
    if (u->left) walkPaths(u->left, cur, out);
    if (u->right) walkPaths(u->right, cur, out);
    cur.resize(cur.size() - add.size());
}
```

:::

#### By value

::: {.form-next}
Each call receives its own string. There is nothing to undo. The two forms must return the same set of paths.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('paths', 'copy')
    assert str(final) == "['1->2->5', '1->3']"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def binary_tree_paths_copy(root):
    out = []

    def walk(u, text):
        text = str(u.val) if not text else text + "->" + str(u.val)
        if u.left is None and u.right is None:
            out.append(text)
            return
        if u.left:
            walk(u.left, text)
        if u.right:
            walk(u.right, text)

    if root:
        walk(root, "")
    return out


got = binary_tree_paths(from_level([1, 2, 3, None, 5]))
assert got == binary_tree_paths_copy(from_level([1, 2, 3, None, 5]))
assert set(got) == {"1->2->5", "1->3"}
assert binary_tree_paths(Node(1)) == ["1"]
```

##### C++

```cpp
void walkCopy(TreeNode* u, string text, vector<string>& out) {
    text = text.empty() ? to_string(u->val) : text + "->" + to_string(u->val);
    if (!u->left && !u->right) { out.push_back(text); return; }
    if (u->left) walkCopy(u->left, text, out);
    if (u->right) walkCopy(u->right, text, out);
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
The shared list is $O(n)$ time plus the size of the output. Copying the string at every node is $O(n \cdot h)$ time. Both use $O(h)$ stack. Here $n \le 100$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- A single node is the string of its value, with no arrow.
- `[1,2,3,null,5]` has two paths. Emitting at an internal node $2$ would add a third, `1->2`, which is not root-to-leaf.
- The order of the two children changes the order of the output. Compare as a set unless the statement fixes the order.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Without the pop, `[1, 2, 3, null, 5]` emits `1->2->5` and then `1->2->5->3`.
- A return from the leaf that skips the pop leaves the node on the list. Pop on every way out.
- Recording a path at a null child emits each leaf twice, and also emits a path that stops at a one-child node.
:::

**Variants.** Keeping only the paths with a given sum is [LC 113 · Path Sum II](https://leetcode.com/problems/path-sum-ii/){difficulty="Medium"}. The smallest string read upward from a leaf is [LC 988 · Smallest String Starting From Leaf](https://leetcode.com/problems/smallest-string-starting-from-leaf/){difficulty="Medium"}. A general tree uses the same list, and a leaf is an empty child list. The single longest path is a height, then one step into a tallest child.
